name: What are the biggest renovation mistakes in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: What mistakes most often cause delays, budget overruns, or rework in older Los Angeles-area houses?
mainEntity.text: What mistakes most often cause delays, budget overruns, or rework in older Los Angeles-area houses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Los Angeles homes can be beautiful, but they often hide conditions that affect cost and timing. The biggest mistakes are starting demolition before the scope is fully defined, assuming the existing systems can support modern appliances, and budgeting too tightly without contingency funds. Other common problems include ordering finishes too late, failing to coordinate design and construction early, and hiring a contractor without checking experience on similar homes. Once walls open, old wiring, plumbing, rot, foundation movement, or patchwork past repairs can appear and force redesign. Homeowners can reduce risk by doing a detailed site review, confirming permit needs early, and asking for a realistic allowance structure. The more the project depends on unknown conditions, the more important it is to plan for surprises instead of pretending they will not happen.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common mistakes are underestimating hidden damage, skipping proper design and permit planning, choosing materials too late, ignoring electrical or plumbing capacity, and hiring based on the lowest bid alone. Older homes often need more investigation before construction than newer homes.
